squash_popularity@2006.rationale: Population-normalised all-player participation is direct empirical evidence for football participation/popularity, but the FIFA Big Count extract is mixed-sex and includes unregistered/casual participation; this is therefore evidence-strength calibration, not a complete popularity rating.

squash_access@2006.rationale: Registered-player intensity is the primary organised-access proxy and club footprint is a secondary structural-access proxy. Association registration/club definitions vary, so the score remains provisional evidence rather than a final access rating.

competition_quality@2023.rationale: Professional-player and club density measure professional ecosystem depth, which informs competition quality, but they do not measure results, league quality or opponent strength directly.

elite_support@2023.rationale: Professional employment and club infrastructure are observable proxies for elite-support capacity, but they do not directly measure funding, medical/science provision, travel or federation technical quality.

unsupported_attributes.development_quality: No canonical normalized source in the current slice directly measures coaching, academies, talent identification or youth pathway quality.
unsupported_attributes.squash_tradition: A 2006/2023 cross-sectional signal cannot measure long-term institutional/cultural continuity.

safeguards: Evidence score is not a canonical country rating.
No recipe may use a signal outside its declared primary dimensions without an explicit model revision.
Missing required components produce a missing evidence score; missing is never zero.
Scores are rounded to one decimal only after component weighting.
No score is extrapolated beyond the declared percentile transfer curve.
A future canonical rating must combine this quantitative evidence with independent historical/context evidence and explicit observation provenance.
